chunks.text: 2.2. Motion control This study adopted a skid steering control for the autonomous ma - neuver of the robot in the orchard. In skid control, steering is achieved through the difference between the velocity of the left and the right motors that drive the tracks/wheels. The error between the left and the right motor speeds results in a change of the vehicle heading, with the yaw angle directly varying with the magnitude of the velocity differ - ence. In case the two velocities are equal, no directional change happens, and the vehicle continues with no lateral deviation. The steering angle is achieved through a fuzzy controller algorithm devel - oped and refined following numerous laboratory and field tests. Unlike proportional-integral (PI) and proportional integral derivative (PID) controllers, fuzzy controllers can be designed to guarantee stable oper - ation despite the change in parameters or motors ( Kumar et al., 2004 ). Fuzzy controllers consist of three main parts; fuzzification, fuzzy reasoning, and defuzzification. These parts represent the input stage, the processing stage, and an output stage. At the input stage, inputs or errors are mapped to the relevant membership functions and truth values. The processing stage invokes each appropriate rule and generates the rules. The output stage transforms the combined result back into a specific control output value. For good performance of the controller the number of parameters should be carefully selected ( Vans et al., 2014 ). In this study, after determination of the offset and the heading of the robot in relation to the medial axis, the velocities of the left and the right tracks were adjusted to steer the robot towards the medial axis (coordinates). Original papers Medial axis-based machine-vision system for orchard robot navigation Samwel Opiyo a , b , Cedric Okinda a , Jun Zhou a , * , Emmy Mwangi a , Nelson Makange a a College of Engineering, Laboratory of Modern Facility Agriculture Technology and Equipment Engineering of Jiangsu Province, Nanjing Agricultural University, Jiangsu 210031, PR China b The Catholic University of Eastern Africa (CUEA), Department of Science, 62157 – 00200 Nairobi, Kenya ARTICLE INFO Keywords: Medial axis Machine vision Precision agriculture Gabor filters Fuzzy logic control ABSTRACT In this paper, we propose a novel medial axis-based machine vision technique for autonomous path tracking and navigation of an agricultural robot in orchards. In the proposed method, the raw color image captured by the onboard camera is converted to grayscale using the color index of vegetation extraction. The gray image is run through Gabor filters to extract the texture features before applying Principal Component Analysis technique to minimize the computational load during path coordinate extraction. The resulting image is clustered using K- means clustering algorithm with k = 2 as proved best based on Silhouette method. Navigation path is then extracted using medial axis algorithm from the binary image generated after k-means clustering. Fuzzy logic controller with two inputs, heading and offset, is used to smoothly track the medial axis during navigation. Experiment is carried out in an orchard environment to gauge the performance of the system. The results of field experiment clearly demonstrate that the proposed medial axis technique has the potential to accurately extract guidance path for robot navigation. The navigation performance of the system is quite satisfactory with a maximum trajectory tracking error and standard deviation of 14.6 mm and 6.8 mm respectively. The average root mean square error ( RMSE ) for the lateral deviation was 45.3 mm. 1. The output stage transforms the combined result back into a specific control output value. In the proposed method, the raw color image captured by the onboard camera is converted to grayscale using the color index of vegetation extraction. The gray image is run through Gabor filters to extract the texture features before applying Principal Component Analysis technique to minimize the computational load during path coordinate extraction. The resulting image is clustered using K- means clustering algorithm with k = 2 as proved best based on Silhouette method. Navigation path is then extracted using medial axis algorithm from the binary image generated after k-means clustering. Fuzzy logic controller with two inputs, heading and offset, is used to smoothly track the medial axis during navigation. Experiment is carried out in an orchard environment to gauge the performance of the system. The results of field experiment clearly demonstrate that the proposed medial axis technique has the potential to accurately extract guidance path for robot navigation. The navigation performance of the system is quite satisfactory with a maximum trajectory tracking error and standard deviation of 14.6 mm and 6.8 mm respectively. The average root mean square error ( RMSE ) for the lateral deviation was 45.3 mm. 1. Fuzzy logic controller with two inputs, heading and offset, is used to smoothly track the medial axis during navigation. Experiment is carried out in an orchard environment to gauge the performance of the system. The results of field experiment clearly demonstrate that the proposed medial axis technique has the potential to accurately extract guidance path for robot navigation. The navigation performance of the system is quite satisfactory with a maximum trajectory tracking error and standard deviation of 14.6 mm and 6.8 mm respectively. Hence, to minimize the computational demand during processing, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) tech - nique was employed. The central idea of PCA is to reduce the dimen - sionality of a data set having a large number of interrelated variables while retaining as much as possible of the variation present in the data set. PCA generates a new set of orthogonal features known as principal components by transforming several interrelated variables ( Jolliffe and Cadima, 2016 ) hence eliminating redundancies. Data clustering using k-means. The final step in the segmenta - tion stage was to classify the data using the k-means algorithm. K-means is reported as among the simplest unsupervised learning algorithms that solve the well-known clustering problem ( Kodinariya and Makwana, 2013; Tian et al., 2019 ). The procedure adopts a simple way to classify a data set through a certain number of clusters fixed a priori. One of the controversial issues in clustering is the determination of the number of clusters appropriate for the data set. There are several techniques employed in determining the number of clusters, including; the rule of thumb ( Madhulatha, 2012 ), Elbow method ( Bholowalia and Kumar, 2014; Umargono et al., 2020 ), Information Criterion Approach ( Boz - dogan, 1994 ), Information-Theoretic Approach ( Sugar and James, 2003 ), Using Silhouette ( Kodinariya and Makwana, 2013; Shahapure and Nicholas, 2020 ) and Cross-validation methods ( Smyth, 1996 ). The silhouette method was selected as it is lighter and gives more reliable results independently ( Ossama et al., 2011 ). Fuzzy logic controller with two inputs, heading and offset, is used to smoothly track the medial axis during navigation. Experiment is carried out in an orchard environment to gauge the performance of the system. The results of field experiment clearly demonstrate that the proposed medial axis technique has the potential to accurately extract guidance path for robot navigation. The navigation performance of the system is quite satisfactory with a maximum trajectory tracking error and standard deviation of 14.6 mm and 6.8 mm respectively.
